prompt: Explain the federal budget using only football metaphors. Do not stop when they stop working.
response:
The federal budget is the ultimate Super Bowl of American finance, but instead of two teams, it's 535 quarterbacks (Congress), one head coach (the President), and 330 million fans who all think they could've called a better game.

Every April, the head coach draws up the playbook—the President's Budget—and hands it off to the offensive line in the House. They huddle up, argue about which plays to run, then lateral it to the Senate where they immediately start running a completely different scheme. This is the budgetary equivalent of the Washington Generals trying to negotiate with the Harlem Globetrotters while both teams are wearing each other's jerseys.

The entire thing is scored in trillions of yards. A trillion dollars is roughly the distance from Earth to the moon if you decided to run there and back while carrying Aaron Donald on your back, stopping every 40 yards to argue about who should pay for the Gatorade.

**Mandatory spending** is like the offensive line: it's huge, it takes up most of the salary cap, and nobody notices it until it fails and the quarterback gets sacked. This includes Social Security (the pension plan for old veterans of the gridiron), Medicare (the team doctor's extremely expensive insurance policy), and interest on the national debt (the league office charging you vigorish for all those years you spent in salary cap hell).

**Discretionary spending** is the skill positions—shiny, exciting, and what everyone argues about during training camp. This is where we decide if we're drafting more F-35s (the defensive ends that cost $100 million each and sometimes can't even make it off the line), funding NASA (sending wide receivers to the moon), or paying for education (teaching the rookies how to read the playbook).

The **budget deficit** is when your team spends the entire season on credit, promising the equipment manager you'll pay him back after you win the Super Bowl. The **national debt** is the cumulative bar tab from every season since 1776, now so large that the interest payments alone could fund an entire expansion franchise.

**Reconciliation** is the budgetary equivalent of using the coach's challenge to overrule the refs, except the refs are in the other locker room wearing the same uniform and also get to challenge your challenge. It's how you ram through the game plan when the other team won't stop blitzing your proposals.
